docs.article:
Upload FBX and OBJ#

Upload the FBX or OBJ your tool already exports — 3ds Max, Maya, Revit, SketchUp, Cinema 4D, Unity, Unreal, Blender — and get a share link. We convert it to glTF on our side, then it takes the same road as a GLB: right-sized, classified, and shown in Fidelity mode (a product) or streamed (a room, a building, a street).

What to upload#

You haveUpload
an FBX with its textures embedded (Max/Maya "Embed Media", Blender "Embed Textures")the .fbx
an FBX whose textures are separate filesa .zip with the .fbx and its texture folder, as the exporter left them
an OBJa .zip with the .obj, its .mtl and the textures. An .obj alone converts, with plain colours
  • FBX: binary or ASCII, FBX 2011–2020 (file versions 7.1–7.7). FBX 2010 and older (6.x) is refused with a message — re-export as FBX 2014 or newer.
  • Zip: standard Deflate or stored entries, no password. Other scene files riding along in the zip (.max, .blend, a USD or glTF copy) are ignored; if both an .fbx and an .obj are inside, the FBX is used (send X-Verse-Kind: obj to pick the OBJ).
  • Texture paths in an FBX or MTL often point at the author's disk (C:\Users\…\Textures\Brick.PNG). They are resolved against the files in the zip by name, case-insensitively, wherever they sit in it.

The same door as every format: drop the file on the upload screen (the FBX and OBJ chips say converted on our side), POST /v1/ingest (the bytes are recognised; X-Verse-Kind: fbx | obj is optional), or @ctruhtech/verse-sdk:

Code
const { job } = await verse.upload(zipFile, { kind: "obj", name: "bistro", units: "cm" });
const rec = await verse.waitForJob(job);
// rec.url     → the share link
// rec.convert → { kind: "obj", schema, products, triangles, materials, images,
//                 missingTextures, units, size, seconds, … }
// rec.fixes   → "Converted the OBJ on our side (from the zip): 1,306 objects, …"

The build shows a converting stage (unpacking the zip → reading the model → writing the glTF), then the usual ladder. Limits are the ordinary ones: 512 MB per upload (a zip counts at its compressed size), 15 minutes for the conversion (VERSE_CONVERT_TIMEOUT_S).

What comes across — and what FBX / OBJ can't carry#

FBXOBJ + MTL
Geometry, normals, UVs, object names and hierarchyyesyes (o objects and g groups become objects)
Unitsfrom the file (UnitScaleFactor): centimetre files from Max / Maya land in metresnone in the format: a model wider than 1,000 units is read as centimetres (wider than 100,000 as millimetres) and the fix line says so; X-Verse-Units: m | cm | mm | in | ft (SDK units) overrides
Up axisfrom the file (UpAxis): Z-up files stand uprightY-up, as the format expects
Base colour, metallic, roughness, emissivePhong / Lambert values; 3ds Max Physical, Maya Stingray PBS and Arnold base values and maps (colour, normal, metalness, roughness, emission) are read from the file and mapped to PBRKd, Ke, the PBR extension lines (Pr, Pm, Ps, Pc) and the map_* textures
Texturesembedded ones always; separate files when zipped. TIFF, TGA, BMP, DDS and EXR are re-encoded as PNGwhen zipped
TransparencyTransparencyFactor / opacity → alphad → alpha. Tf (transmission filter) is not turned into glass — most exporters write Tf 1 1 1 by default
Animation and skinsnode animation and skinned meshes play (one clip with every moving object in it); static "Take 001" takes are dropped so a still scene is not published as animated— (OBJ has none)
Lights and cameraslights come across; cameras are not used—
Not carriedrenderer-only shaders (V-Ray, Corona, Redshift, Arnold node graphs beyond their base values), procedural maps, displacement, layered materials, photometric (IES) lights, more than one animation take, morph targets (shape keys are kept in the file but the streamed viewer does not play them)anything beyond the MTL

Emission strength and the clearcoat of a 3ds Max Physical / Stingray / Arnold material become the matching KHR_materials_* extensions and render as listed in what is rendered. Phong specular is not PBR data: it is set to the neutral value rather than turned into KHR_materials_specular.

Missing textures never fail an upload: the link builds, those surfaces keep their colour, and the record names them (convert.missingTextures, and the fix line: "3 textures the model names were not in the upload (Brick_Diff.png, …) — upload a .zip with the texture folder to include them").

How the conversion works (and why Blender)#

tools/model-convert/convert.mjs unpacks a zip (zip-slip and zip-bomb guarded), transcodes an ASCII FBX to binary, repairs MTL texture paths, and runs headless Blender 5.0 (blender -b) to import the model and export glTF. Blender reads binary FBX only, so the ASCII→binary step is our own (fbx-ascii.mjs): ASCII and binary FBX are the same node tree, so the transcode is lossless — it keeps the 3ds Max Physical and Stingray properties that an importer round trip would drop.

We measured three converters on the same files before choosing (the gate fixture: a textured cube, a metallic sphere, an emissive lamp and a skinned, animated bar, exported metres Y-up and centimetres Z-up; the Unity Boat Attack FBX files from 3ds Max; and the Intel Sponza release, a 929 MB ASCII FBX with 3ds Max Physical materials, 3.75 M triangles and 144 textures):

Blender 5.0 (chosen)FBX2glTF 0.13 (FBX SDK 2020)assimp 6.0
Units and up axis (cm Z-up fixture → 5 × 2.15 × 2 m)correctcorrect100× too big (500 × 215 × 200: no FBX unit conversion)
Materials on the fixturegold metallic 1 / roughness 0.3, lamp emission ×4 — exactmetallic 0.4 on every material, roughness from shininess (0.2), duplicated materialstexture darkened (base factor 0.8), metallic lost, extra specular/volume extensions
Materials on Unity / Max filessane Phong mappingthe Unity cliffs glow white (emissive 1)roughness −0.6 (invalid)
ASCII FBXvia our lossless transcoderread, but the external texture was lostread
OBJcorrect (cm OBJ read as cm by rule)100× too small (0.05 m)correct, but a phantom default material
Animation / skinskept (one clip)kept (1-channel stubs per take)kept
Sponza 929 MB ASCII FBX72 s, 3.5 GB peak (zip in, all 28 Physical materials mapped, 95 maps incl. normal / roughness / metalness, 36.2 × 19.9 × 23.8 m)182 s (x86 build under Rosetta), 2.9 GB, 49 maps, base colour halved26 s but 7.2 GB, 3,625 m wide, roughness −2.2
Fixture conversion0.5–1 s, 220 MB0.05–0.12 s, 14 MB0.01–0.03 s, 7 MB
In the image+360 MB compressed (pruned Linux build)+6 MB, but bundles the proprietary Autodesk FBX SDK; x86-only+10 MB

Blender is the slowest and largest, and the only one that got units, axes and materials right on every file — the criteria that decide whether the link looks like the model. The image cost is in the "In the image" row above.

When it does not work#

MessageWhyWhat to do
This FBX or OBJ file isn't one we can read (model_invalid)not FBX/OBJ bytes, FBX older than 2011, a zip with no .fbx/.obj, an unreadable filere-export (FBX 2014+ binary is the safest), or zip the model itself
We couldn't convert this file (convert_failed)the converter crashed or ran past 15 minutestry again; if it repeats, export GLB from your tool
the model is 100× too big or too smallan OBJ in a unit the rule guessed wrongupload again with X-Verse-Units (SDK units)
surfaces are flat coloursthe textures were separate files and not zipped, or the MTL was missingzip the model with its texture folder (and .mtl)
